sections.heading: Also here
steps: Repair a system that will not start, and Upgrade to the next version, have their own guides.

title: Securing a Windows computer
summary: Checking antivirus, firewall, encryption, updates and accounts, and fixing what is off.

steps.t: On the Dashboard, under Other fixes, click Run beside Security checkup, then Start.
steps.tip: Restart MendKit as administrator first so Secure Boot can be checked.

steps.t: Read each line.
steps.see: One result each for antivirus, firewall, drive encryption, account protection and SmartScreen, Windows Update, Secure Boot, administrator accounts and remote access. Each red or amber line says what to do.

sections.heading: Fix in one run

steps.t: Tick Technician mode, open Repair, and run Secure this computer.
steps.see: A restore point first, then: firewall on, Defender on (unless another antivirus is protecting the computer), Defender updated, User Account Control and SmartScreen back to normal, Windows Update resumed, Guest account off, then the checkup again.

steps: Restart if the results ask you to.

sections.heading: Fixes that are not automatic

steps.t: Remote Desktop: if nobody connects to this computer remotely, run "Turn off Remote Desktop" from Repair.
steps.warn: If a technician or employer connects with Remote Desktop, leave it on.

steps: SMBv1: run "Turn off SMBv1" unless a very old network drive or a printer that scans to a folder needs it. Restart afterwards.

steps.t: Drive encryption: on Windows Pro, Settings, Privacy & security, Device encryption or BitLocker. Save the recovery key to the person's Microsoft account first.
steps.warn: Without the recovery key, an encrypted drive cannot be read if Windows breaks.

steps: Secure Boot: turn it on in the computer's firmware settings (usually F2 or Del at start-up, under Boot or Security).

sections.heading: After a scam
steps: Run the remote access audit and Pop-ups or strange behaviour as well. See "Staying safe: scams and fake support".

title: Upgrading to Windows 11
summary: Checking whether a Windows 10 computer can run Windows 11, fixing what can be fixed, and doing the upgrade without losing anything.
time: 15 minutes, plus an hour for the upgrade

sections.heading: Before you start

steps.t: Back up the person's files first: Migrate, Back up to a drive.
steps.tip: The upgrade keeps files, apps and settings, but a power cut or a failing drive in the middle can lose them.

steps.t: Restart MendKit as administrator (Dashboard, Restart as administrator, then Yes).
steps.tip: Without it, the security chip (TPM), the start-up mode and BitLocker cannot be read.

steps: Plug a laptop into power. Allow about an hour for the upgrade itself.

steps.t: Open the Windows 11 upgrade: from the Dashboard notice, or tick Technician mode, open Repair, and click Open beside Windows 11 upgrade under Windows tools.
steps.see: After a few seconds: one line per requirement, each green, amber or red, with a button where something can be fixed.

steps.t: Read "Windows' own check" first.
steps.see: This is the same answer Windows Update uses. If it says Windows has not checked yet, click Ask Windows to check and wait a few minutes.

steps.t: Read the rest.
steps.tip: A red line with a button can be fixed. A red line without one (an old processor, too little memory) is the hardware itself.

sections.heading: Fixes

steps.t: No TPM found, on a newer processor: click Restart into firmware settings, then click it again.
steps.see: The computer restarts into its firmware (BIOS) settings in 10 seconds.
steps.tip: Look under Security, Advanced or Trusted Computing for Intel PTT, AMD fTPM, Security Device Support or TPM, and set it to Enabled. Save and exit, usually with F10.

steps.t: Old BIOS (Legacy) start-up on an MBR drive: click Convert the drive to GPT, then click it again.
steps.see: The result says Converted. Then click Restart into firmware settings, set Boot Mode to UEFI and turn off CSM or Legacy Support, and turn on Secure Boot. Save and exit.
steps.warn: After converting, the computer will not start until the firmware is switched to UEFI. Have the BitLocker recovery key ready if the drive is encrypted. Microsoft's tool checks first and changes nothing if it is not safe.

steps: Not enough free space: click Free up space. The upgrade needs about 30 GB.
After any fix, click Check again at the top, and Ask Windows to check for Windows' own answer.

steps.t: When the top says the computer is ready, click Start the upgrade.
steps.see: MendKit downloads Microsoft's Windows 11 Installation Assistant, checks that Microsoft signed it, and opens it.

steps.t: In the Installation Assistant, click Accept and install.
steps.see: It downloads Windows 11, prepares it, then asks to restart. The computer restarts a few times; the screen says not to turn it off.

steps.t: Sign in when it is done and check the person's files, email and printer.
steps.tip: For 10 days, Settings, System, Recovery, Go back returns to Windows 10.

sections.heading: If the computer cannot run Windows 11
steps: Keep Windows 10 with Extended Security Updates: free for home computers until 12 October 2027. Open Windows Update and click Enroll now. It may ask to sign in with a Microsoft account or turn on Windows Backup.
Switch to Linux with the Switch to Linux assistant: free and supported for years.

steps.t: Upgrade anyway: when the only problem is the processor (and the computer has at least a TPM 1.2 chip), click Allow the upgrade, then get the Windows 11 ISO from the ISO Library, open it and run setup.exe.
steps.warn: Microsoft does not support this. The computer may not get every update, and a desktop watermark may appear. Back up first.

steps: Or replace the computer. "Is this computer worth fixing?" on the Dashboard weighs it up.

title: Start a Mac in Safe Mode
summary: Starting macOS with only Apple's own software, to find out whether an app or add-on is behind a problem.

sections.heading: Apple silicon (M1 and later)
steps: Click the Apple menu and choose Shut Down. Wait 10 seconds after the screen goes dark.

steps.t: Press and hold the power button (Touch ID button on a laptop). Keep holding.
steps.see: "Loading startup options", then the startup disk and an Options gear.

steps: Click the startup disk (usually Macintosh HD). Hold Shift and click Continue in Safe Mode, then let go of Shift.

steps.t: Sign in. You may be asked to sign in twice.
steps.see: "Safe Boot" in red at the top right of the login window.

sections.heading: Intel Macs
steps: Restart the Mac and immediately press and hold Shift.

steps.t: Let go when the login window appears. Sign in, possibly twice.
steps.see: "Safe Boot" at the top right of the login window.

sections.heading: What it tells you
steps: If the problem is gone in Safe Mode, something installed is causing it. Restart normally and use Startup items in MendKit to remove leftovers and unknown items.
If the problem is still there, it is more likely macOS itself or hardware: try "macOS Recovery and First Aid", then MendKit's hardware tests.
Safe Mode also checks the startup disk and clears some caches, so a normal restart afterwards sometimes fixes things on its own.
Safe Mode is slower and some features (graphics effects, some Wi-Fi and audio) may not work. That is normal.
To leave Safe Mode, restart normally.

title: macOS Recovery and First Aid
summary: Repairing the startup disk from outside macOS, and reinstalling macOS without erasing files.

sections.heading: Open Recovery
steps: Apple silicon: shut down. Press and hold the power button until "Loading startup options" appears. Click Options, then Continue.
Intel: restart and immediately hold Command and R until the Apple logo appears.

steps.t: Choose a user and type its password if asked.
steps.see: macOS Recovery with Restore from Time Machine, Reinstall macOS, Safari and Disk Utility.

sections.heading: Repair the disk with First Aid
steps: Choose Disk Utility and click Continue.

steps.t: Click View in the toolbar and choose Show All Devices.
steps.see: The internal disk, its container, and volumes such as Macintosh HD and Macintosh HD - Data.

steps.t: Select the last volume in the list, click First Aid, then Run.
steps.tip: Work upwards: each volume, then the container, then the disk itself.

steps.t: If it says it repaired something, run it again until it finds no problems.
steps.warn: "First Aid failed" or "unable to repair" on the disk itself: copy the files off now and plan to replace or erase the drive.

sections.heading: Reinstall macOS and keep files
steps: Quit Disk Utility. Choose Reinstall macOS and click Continue.

steps.t: Choose the startup disk (Macintosh HD) and follow the steps.
steps.see: A progress bar. It takes 30 minutes to over an hour and restarts several times.
steps.tip: Keep a laptop on its charger and connected to the internet. Files, apps and settings stay.

sections.heading: Restore from Time Machine
steps: Restore from Time Machine puts the whole Mac back as it was at a backup time. It replaces what is there now.

title: Reset NVRAM and SMC on Intel Macs
summary: Clearing the stored settings behind startup, sound, display, fan and power problems on Intel Macs. Apple-silicon Macs do this themselves on a restart.

sections.heading: When it helps
steps: Fans running flat out, a battery that will not charge, a Mac that will not wake from sleep, the wrong startup disk, sound or display settings that keep resetting, or power and lights acting oddly.

steps.t: Apple menu, About This Mac. "Chip: Apple M..." means Apple silicon: just shut down, wait 30 seconds and start it again. "Processor: Intel" means follow these steps.
ex: Chip: Apple M2   → Apple silicon: a shut down and restart does both resets
Processor: 2.3 GHz Quad-Core Intel Core i5   → an Intel Mac: use the key steps below

sections.heading: Reset NVRAM (PRAM)
steps: Shut the Mac down.

steps.t: Press the power button, then immediately press and hold Option, Command, P and R together.
ex: Press the power button, then within a second hold all four: Option (⌥), Command (⌘), P and R. Your left hand takes Option and Command, your right hand P and R.

steps.t: Keep holding for about 20 seconds. On a Mac with a T2 chip, let go after the Apple logo appears and disappears a second time. On older Macs, let go after the second startup sound.
ex: Without a T2 chip you hear the startup chime a second time; let go after it. Macs from 2018 to 2020 have a T2 chip: watch for the Apple logo to appear and disappear twice.

steps: Afterwards, check the startup disk (System Settings, General, Startup Disk), display resolution, sound volume and time zone.

sections.heading: Reset the SMC: laptops with a T2 chip (2018 to 2020)
steps: Shut down. Press and hold Control, Option and Shift on the left side for 7 seconds.
Keep holding them and also press and hold the power button for another 7 seconds.
Let go of everything, wait a few seconds, and press the power button to start the Mac.

sections.heading: Reset the SMC: other laptops (non-removable battery, before 2018)
steps: Shut down. Hold Shift, Control and Option on the left side and the power button, all together, for 10 seconds.
Let go and press the power button.

sections.heading: Reset the SMC: desktops (iMac, Mac mini, Mac Pro)
steps: Shut down and unplug the power cord. Wait 15 seconds.
Plug it back in, wait 5 seconds, and press the power button.

title: Make a bootable macOS USB installer
summary: A USB stick that installs or reinstalls macOS without the internet or a working Recovery.
need: A USB stick of 32 GB or more
An administrator password

steps.t: In MendKit, open Repair and run "Download the macOS installer". Type your password.
steps.see: "Install macOS ..." appears in Applications. It is over 12 GB, so allow time.
steps.tip: For a specific older version, use Apple's support page "How to download and install macOS". "macOS installers available" lists what Apple offers this Mac.

sections.heading: Make the stick

steps.t: Plug in a USB stick of 32 GB or more.
steps.warn: Everything on the stick will be erased.

steps: Open Disk Utility (Applications, Utilities). Click View, Show All Devices. Select the stick (the top line for it, with its maker's name).
Click Erase. Name: MyVolume. Format: Mac OS Extended (Journaled). Scheme: GUID Partition Map. Click Erase.

steps.t: Open Terminal (see "Opening Terminal and typing a command") and type, replacing Sequoia with the name of the installer you downloaded:
steps.see: sudo /Applications/Install\ macOS\ Sequoia.app/Contents/Resources/createinstallmedia --volume /Volumes/MyVolume

steps.t: Press Return, type your Mac password (nothing shows as you type) and press Return. Type Y and press Return when asked.
steps.see: "Erasing disk", "Copying to disk" with percentages, then "Install media now available". It takes 10 to 30 minutes.

steps: Eject the stick in Finder before unplugging it.

sections.heading: Start from it
steps: Apple silicon: shut down, hold the power button until startup options appear, choose the installer and click Continue.

steps.t: Intel: restart holding Option and choose the installer.
steps.tip: Macs with a T2 chip need "Allow booting from external media" in Startup Security Utility first (Recovery, Utilities).

title: Mac battery checks
summary: Reading a Mac's battery condition, making it last longer, and knowing when it needs replacing.

steps.t: In MendKit, run Battery from the Repair screen, or run the Health report.
steps.see: Cycle count, condition and Maximum Capacity. Under 80% is flagged as due for replacement.

steps.t: Or open System Settings, Battery, and click the info button next to Battery Health.
steps.see: Normal, or Service Recommended.

sections.heading: Make it last longer between charges
steps: Turn on Optimised Battery Charging in Battery settings.
In MendKit Repair, run "Turn off Power Nap" and "Set sensible sleep timers".
Run the "Runs hot or shuts down" recipe: an app keeping the processor busy drains the battery fast.
Lower the screen brightness; it is the biggest single drain.

sections.heading: When to stop using it

steps.t: A swollen battery lifts the trackpad, makes the bottom case bulge or stops the laptop sitting flat.
steps.warn: Stop using and charging the Mac and have the battery replaced right away. Swollen batteries can catch fire. Do not press on it.

steps: Sudden shutdowns at 20 to 40% charge mean a worn battery. "Why did it shut down?" in MendKit confirms it.

title: Installing MendKit on Linux
summary: Which download to pick for each Linux, and how to install it.

sections.heading: Pick the right file
steps: Ubuntu, Linux Mint, Debian, Pop!_OS, Zorin OS, elementary OS: the .deb package.
Fedora, openSUSE, Nobara: the .rpm package.
Anything else (Arch, Manjaro, Void and others): the AppImage, which runs without installing.

sections.heading: Install the .deb (Ubuntu, Mint and similar)
steps: Download the .deb from the MendKit website.

steps.t: Open the Downloads folder and double-click the file.
steps.see: The Software app (or Package Installer on Mint) with an Install button.

steps.t: Click Install and type your password.
steps.tip: Or in Terminal: sudo apt install ./Downloads/MendKit-*.deb

steps: Open MendKit from the applications menu.

sections.heading: Install the .rpm (Fedora, openSUSE)
steps: Download the .rpm and double-click it, then click Install. Or in Terminal: sudo dnf install ./Downloads/MendKit-*.rpm (openSUSE: sudo zypper install ./Downloads/MendKit-*.rpm).

sections.heading: Run the AppImage
steps: Download the AppImage. Right-click it, choose Properties, then Permissions, and tick "Allow executing file as program" (or run chmod +x on it).

steps.t: Double-click it.
steps.warn: On Ubuntu 22.04 and later the AppImage will not open until one extra package is installed. Run: sudo apt install libfuse2t64 (on 22.04: sudo apt install libfuse2). The .deb does not need this.

title: Switching a computer from Windows 10 to Linux
summary: Moving a Windows 10 computer that cannot run Windows 11 to Linux Mint, from the first check to the restored files.
need: A USB stick of 8 GB or more
An external drive for the backup
A network cable if the Wi-Fi card is Broadcom

sections.heading: Why and when
steps: Windows 10 stopped getting security updates in October 2025. Computers that cannot run Windows 11 keep working, but become less safe each month.
Linux Mint is free, gets updates for years, and looks and works much like Windows: a Start-style menu, a taskbar, a file manager and the usual apps.

It suits people who mostly use a web browser, email, documents, photos and video calls. It does not suit people who rely on Windows-only programs (some accounting, CAD and games with anti-cheat) unless those work in a browser.

sections.heading: 1. Check the computer with MendKit

steps.t: On the Windows computer, open MendKit. Click Switch to Linux on the Dashboard notice, or open Repair (Technician mode) and click Switch to Linux.
steps.see: After a minute or two: a verdict, the hardware checks, and a table of each app and what replaces it on Linux.

steps: Read every amber and red item. Broadcom Wi-Fi or NVIDIA graphics are fine but need a step after installing; a 32-bit processor or under 2 GB of memory is not worth it.

steps.t: Go through the apps table with the owner.
steps.tip: Programs with no Linux version and no browser version are the deal-breakers. Decide now, not after Windows is gone.

sections.heading: 2. Back up everything

steps.t: Plug in an external drive. In MendKit, click Back up to a drive and back up every user.
steps.tip: See "Backing up to a drive and restoring".

steps: Make sure browser passwords are synced to the person's account or exported (Move saved passwords).
Write down the Wi-Fi password, and any licence keys for programs that will be reinstalled.
Check the backup: open the drive and open a few documents and photos from it.

sections.heading: 3. Make the USB stick
steps: Open ISO Library and download Linux Mint (Cinnamon edition; the Xfce edition for computers with under 4 GB of memory).

steps.t: Write it to a USB stick of 8 GB or more with Rufus, or copy it onto a Ventoy stick.
steps.tip: See the Rufus and Ventoy guides.

steps.t: Plug the stick into the computer and start from it (see "Starting a computer from a USB stick").
steps.see: The Mint start menu. Choose the first option, Start Linux Mint.

steps.t: Wait for the desktop.
steps.see: A full Linux Mint desktop running from the stick. Nothing on the drive has changed yet.

steps.t: Check the things that matter: connect to Wi-Fi (network icon at the bottom right), play a video for sound, check the screen, touchpad and webcam.
steps.tip: If Wi-Fi is missing, the card needs a driver: plug in a network cable for the install, and run Missing drivers afterwards.

sections.heading: 5. Install
steps: Double-click Install Linux Mint on the desktop.
Choose the language and keyboard layout, and click Continue.
Connect to Wi-Fi if asked. Tick "Install multimedia codecs" and click Continue.

steps.t: Installation type: choose "Erase disk and install Linux Mint" to replace Windows.
steps.warn: This deletes everything on the drive, including Windows and every file. Only continue once the backup is checked. To keep Windows, choose "Install Linux Mint alongside Windows" instead; each start then offers a choice.

steps: Click Install Now, then Continue to confirm the changes.
Choose the time zone on the map.

steps.t: Type the person's name, the computer's name, a user name and a password. Leave "Require my password to log in" selected.
steps.tip: This password is also the administrator password Linux asks for when installing updates. Write it down for the owner.

steps.t: Wait for the installation, about 10 to 20 minutes. Click Restart Now, remove the USB stick when asked and press Enter.
steps.see: Linux Mint starts from the drive, with a Welcome Screen.

sections.heading: 6. Finish setting it up
steps: In the Welcome Screen, click First Steps and open Driver Manager to install any recommended drivers (NVIDIA, Broadcom). Restart if it installs any.
Install MendKit (see "Installing MendKit on Linux").

In MendKit, run the recipe "First setup after installing Linux". It installs updates, drivers, codecs, Office-compatible fonts, printer drivers, and turns on the firewall and automatic security updates.
Open Setup Profiles and apply "New Linux computer": Firefox, Thunderbird, LibreOffice, VLC, Timeshift and the Standard tweaks.
Plug in the backup drive. Open Migrate, Restore from a drive, and restore the files. Then click Reinstall apps from the old computer.
Set up Timeshift (see its guide) so the system can be rolled back after a bad update.
Sign in to the browser, email and cloud accounts with the owner, and show them the menu, the Software Manager and the Update Manager.

title: First setup after installing Linux
summary: Finishing a fresh Linux install with one recipe and one setup profile.

sections.heading: What the recipe does
steps: Installs all updates, finds devices without a driver and installs the recommended drivers and firmware.
Installs media codecs (MP4, MP3, H.264 and more), turns on Flathub in the Software app, installs fonts that match Microsoft's so Office documents keep their layout, and installs printer drivers.
Turns on the firewall and automatic security updates, then reports the security settings.

sections.heading: How to run it
steps: Install and open MendKit. Tick Technician mode and click Repair.

steps.t: Find "First setup after installing Linux" and click Run, then Start. Type your password when asked.
steps.see: About 15 to 40 minutes depending on the number of updates.

steps: Restart when it finishes.
Open Setup Profiles and click Apply to this computer on "New Linux computer".
Check sound, Wi-Fi, a printer and a video, then restore the files from the backup.

sections.heading: Notes
steps: On Fedora, codecs come from the RPM Fusion repositories, which the recipe adds.
On Debian, firmware needs the "non-free-firmware" component turned on in Software & Updates.
The Microsoft fonts installer accepts Microsoft's licence for you on Ubuntu and Mint.

title: Linux: missing drivers, NVIDIA graphics and Wi-Fi
summary: Finding hardware without a driver and installing the right one, including NVIDIA graphics and Broadcom Wi-Fi.

steps.t: In MendKit, run the recipe "Missing drivers" (or "Graphics or Wi-Fi not working right" on the Dashboard).
steps.see: Devices with no driver, firmware that failed to load, and the graphics and network chips.

steps.t: The recipe runs "Install recommended drivers", which installs what Ubuntu suggests (NVIDIA, Broadcom and others). Restart afterwards.
steps.tip: Mint's own Driver Manager (in the menu) does the same, with a choice of versions.

sections.heading: NVIDIA on Fedora
steps: Run "Install the NVIDIA driver (Fedora)". It adds RPM Fusion and installs the driver, which then builds itself (about 5 minutes).

steps.t: If Secure Boot is on, the results say so. Restart.
steps.see: A blue screen, Perform MOK management. Choose Enroll MOK, then Continue, Yes, type the password you were given, and Reboot.
steps.warn: If you skip this screen, the NVIDIA driver will not load. Run the command again to get another chance.

sections.heading: Broadcom Wi-Fi
steps: Connect the computer to the internet another way: a network cable, or a phone shared over USB (on the phone, turn on USB tethering).
Run "Install the Broadcom Wi-Fi driver", then restart. Wi-Fi networks appear in the network menu.

sections.heading: Firmware
steps: "Install missing firmware" installs the firmware package most Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and graphics chips need. On Debian, turn on the non-free-firmware component first.

title: Repairing a Linux system that will not start
summary: Using a Linux live USB and MendKit to check the drive and rebuild the startup menu and startup files.
need: A Linux live USB stick
Internet on the broken computer

sections.heading: Try these first

steps.t: At power-on, hold Shift (or tap Esc on newer systems) to show the GRUB startup menu. Choose Advanced options and an older kernel.
steps.tip: If that works, the newest kernel is the problem: update again later, or run "Always show the startup menu" so the older one is always one key away.

steps: Stuck at a black screen or "emergency mode" after an update: restore a Timeshift snapshot, or use the steps below with "Rebuild the startup files".

sections.heading: Start from a live USB
steps: Make a Ubuntu or Linux Mint USB stick (ISO Library and Rufus or Ventoy). It does not have to match the installed Linux.
Start the broken computer from it and choose Try or Start Linux Mint, not Install.
Connect to the internet (needed for Fedora, and to download MendKit).
Download the MendKit AppImage from the website. Open Terminal and type: sudo apt install libfuse2t64 (on 22.04: libfuse2). Then make the AppImage runnable and open it.

sections.heading: Repair with MendKit

steps.t: Tick Technician mode, open Repair, and click Open beside Repair a system that will not start.
steps.see: The partitions found, and notices for encrypted or LVM drives.

steps: Encrypted drive: open the Files app, click the encrypted drive and type its password, then reopen the screen. LVM: click Look for LVM partitions.

steps.t: Choose the installed system's partition, usually the largest ext4 or btrfs one.
steps.tip: MendKit checks it really holds an installed Linux before changing anything.

steps: Leave "Check and repair the file system" and "Reinstall and rebuild the startup menu" ticked. Tick "Rebuild the startup files" too if it stopped at a black screen or emergency mode.

steps.t: Click Repair it and type the live system's password if asked (often none: just press Enter).
steps.see: Results for the file system check and for the startup repair, naming the installed system.

steps: Shut down, remove the USB stick and start the computer.

sections.heading: If it still will not start
steps: The drive itself may be failing: check it with smartmontools from the live session, and copy the files off with MendKit's "Copy from an old drive".
Windows updates sometimes take over the startup order on dual-boot computers: in the computer's startup menu (F12 and similar), choose the Linux entry (ubuntu, Mint or Fedora).

title: Upgrading Linux to the next version
summary: Moving Ubuntu, Linux Mint or Fedora to its next release safely.

sections.heading: When
steps: MendKit's Dashboard warns when a version is close to or past the end of its security updates.
Ubuntu LTS and Linux Mint versions get 5 years of updates; Fedora about 13 months, so Fedora needs upgrading every year.

sections.heading: Get ready

steps.t: Open Repair and click Open beside Upgrade to the next version.
steps.see: Checks: free space (15 GB needed), mains power, waiting updates, a Timeshift snapshot, extra software sources, and the end of support date.

steps: Fix anything red. Install waiting updates in the Updates screen and restart.

steps.t: Take a Timeshift snapshot and back up personal files.
steps.warn: Upgrades usually go smoothly, but a power cut or a full drive mid-way can leave the computer unable to start.

sections.heading: Ubuntu and Linux Mint

steps.t: Click Start the upgrade.
steps.see: Ubuntu: the Software Updater offers the new version; click Upgrade. Mint: the Mint upgrade tool opens.

steps: Follow its screens. It asks for your password, checks again, downloads (30 to 90 minutes) and asks before replacing settings files: keep the current version unless you know otherwise.
Restart when it finishes. Extra software sources were turned off: turn them back on in Software & Updates (or Software Sources on Mint) if needed.

steps.t: Click Download Fedora N.
steps.see: MendKit installs current updates, then downloads the new release. The results list any package in the way.

steps.t: Save your work, then click Restart and upgrade.
steps.see: The computer restarts into an upgrade screen with a progress bar (30 to 60 minutes) and restarts again into the new Fedora.

title: Everyday Linux fixes
summary: Quick fixes for the problems Linux users run into most, and which MendKit recipe or command does each.

sections.heading: Desktop frozen or panel gone
steps: Dashboard: "The desktop froze or the panel vanished". It restarts Cinnamon, KDE Plasma, XFCE or MATE without closing your windows.
GNOME on Wayland cannot be restarted that way: sign out and back in. If nothing responds, press Ctrl, Alt and F3, sign in, and type: sudo systemctl restart gdm

sections.heading: Updates fail
steps: Recipe "Updates fail" handles "could not get lock" (waits for a running update, then finishes half-installed packages), broken extra sources (lists them; "Turn off broken software sources" sets them aside), held packages, Arch's expired signing keys and Snap updates.
Fedora: "Undo the last update (dnf)" rolls back an update that broke something.

sections.heading: No sound or wrong output
steps: Recipe "No sound" restarts the sound system, then "Reset the sound system completely" clears saved device choices. Afterwards, choose the output in Sound settings.

sections.heading: Printer or scanner
steps: Printers: "Install printer drivers" and "Install HP printer drivers". Most network printers work without a driver: "Printers on the network" lists them.
Scanners: Dashboard "The scanner does not work" installs scanner support, including network scanners.

sections.heading: Keeps asking to unlock the keyring
steps: Happens after a password change. Run "Keeps asking to unlock the keyring" (Repair) and sign out and in.

steps.t: Passwords saved in the old keyring (some apps and Chrome) must be typed again.
steps.warn: The old keyring is kept as a backup, but it needs the old password to open.

sections.heading: Screen problems
steps: Screen sharing or remote support shows black, or an older app misbehaves: try the X11 session (cog on the sign-in screen), or "Use X11 instead of Wayland (GNOME)".
Tearing lines in videos on XFCE: the "Stop screen tearing" tweak. On other desktops, try the Wayland session.
Text too small: the "Larger text" tweak for your desktop.

sections.heading: Slow to start
steps: Dashboard "It takes ages to start" shows which services hold startup up. NetworkManager-wait-online is the usual culprit on desktops; turn it off in Startup items.

sections.heading: Out of space
steps: Repair, Free up space: caches, downloaded update files, old logs, old kernels, old Snap versions, unused Flatpak parts, Docker and Timeshift snapshots, and large files to look at.

title: Securing a Linux computer
summary: Checking and fixing the firewall, automatic updates, remote login and remote access programs.

steps.t: Run the recipe "Linux security checkup".
steps.see: Firewall, automatic security updates, remote login (SSH), who has administrator rights, disk encryption and which programs accept network connections.

sections.heading: Fix

steps.t: Run "Secure this computer". It turns on the firewall (blocking incoming connections only) and automatic security updates.
steps.tip: If remote login (SSH) is in use, MendKit keeps it allowed through the firewall.

steps: If SSH is on and nobody logs in remotely, turn it off: sudo systemctl disable --now ssh
Check the administrators listed are people who should have that power.

sections.heading: Remote access programs
steps: Check for remote access (Dashboard) now removes AnyDesk, TeamViewer, RustDesk and others on Linux too: it stops their services, uninstalls the package or Flatpak and sets loose copies aside.

sections.heading: Encryption
steps: Disk encryption can only be turned on by reinstalling, with "Encrypt the new Linux installation" ticked in the installer. Worth it for laptops.

title: 7-Zip
summary: Opens and makes zip, 7z, rar and other compressed files.

sections.heading: What it is
steps: 7-Zip opens almost any compressed file (zip, 7z, rar, tar, iso) and can make zip or 7z files, with a password if wanted.

sections.heading: When to use it
steps: A download ends in .7z or .rar and Windows cannot open it.
Packing a folder into one file to email or copy.

sections.heading: Install it

steps.t: Open MendKit. At the bottom left of its window, tick the Technician mode box.
steps.see: Repair, Tools and Tweaks appear in the menu on the left. If they were already there, Technician mode was already on.

steps.t: Click Tools in the menu on the left. Click the search box at the top of the list and type 7-Zip.
steps.see: The list shrinks to the row for 7-Zip: a tick box, its name, what it is for, its licence and a Status column saying Not installed or Installed.
ex: Part of the name is enough: "7-Z" finds the same row.

steps.t: Tick the box at the start of the 7-Zip row, then click Install selected at the top of the list.
steps.see: The panel at the bottom of MendKit shows each step of the download and install as it happens. It usually takes one to five minutes.
steps.tip: On Windows, click "Restart as administrator" on the Dashboard first, so installs do not stop half-way to ask permission. On a Mac or Linux, MendKit asks for your password once; nothing shows on screen as you type it, which is normal.

steps.t: Wait until the Status column for 7-Zip says Installed and the bottom panel says the job has finished.
steps.tip: If it failed, check the internet connection and click Install selected again; a second try often works when a download was interrupted. The full reason is in Reports, in the newest Install report.

steps.t: Windows: click the Start button (the Windows logo at the bottom of the screen), type 7-Zip and click it when it appears at the top of the list.
steps.see: 7-Zip opens in its own window. If a box asks "Do you want to allow this app to make changes to your device?", click Yes. That box is Windows checking with you, not an error.
steps.tip: If 7-Zip does not appear straight away, wait a few seconds and type the name again, or look under All apps in the Start menu.

steps: On a Mac and on Linux, 7-Zip has no window: you type its commands in Terminal. See the guide "Opening Terminal and typing a command" if you have not done this before.

steps.t: Windows: right-click the compressed file, choose Show more options, then 7-Zip, then Extract to "folder name\". On Windows 10 the 7-Zip entry is in the first right-click menu; on Windows 11 it is under Show more options.
steps.see: A new folder beside the file with its contents.
steps.tip: If it asks for a password, the sender set one; ask them for it.
ex: Right-click photos-2023.7z → Show more options → 7-Zip → Extract to "photos-2023\"
Result: a new folder called photos-2023 in the same place, with the files inside.

steps.t: To make one: right-click a file or folder, Show more options, 7-Zip, Add to "name.zip".
steps.tip: Zip files open on any computer without extra software. 7z files are smaller but need 7-Zip or a similar program to open.
ex: Right-click the folder Tax 2024 → Show more options → 7-Zip → Add to "Tax 2024.zip"
For a password: choose Add to archive..., type the password twice under Encryption, choose AES-256 and click OK.

steps.t: On a Mac and Linux, 7-Zip is a Terminal command: 7zz x file.7z (Mac) or 7z x file.7z (Linux) extracts into the current folder.
ex: First go to the folder with the file:
> cd ~/Downloads
Extract (Mac):
> 7zz x photos-2023.7z
Extract (Linux):
> 7z x photos-2023.7z
Make a zip of a folder:
> 7z a Tax-2024.zip "Tax 2024"

sections.heading: If something goes wrong
steps: "Wrong password" or "Data error": the file is incomplete or damaged. Download it again.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Compressed files from unknown senders can hide malware. Scan them first.

title: AdwCleaner
summary: Removes adware, browser hijackers and pushy "optimiser" programs.

sections.heading: What it is
steps: AdwCleaner is a small Malwarebytes tool aimed at adware: toolbars, changed home pages and search engines, and unwanted browser add-ons. It runs without installing anything else.

sections.heading: When to use it
steps: The browser's home page or search engine keeps changing.
Ads appear where they should not.

steps.t: Open MendKit. At the bottom left of its window, tick the Technician mode box.
steps.see: Repair, Tools and Tweaks appear in the menu on the left. If they were already there, Technician mode was already on.

steps.see: The list shrinks to the row for AdwCleaner: a tick box, its name, what it is for, its licence and a Status column saying Not installed or Installed.
ex: Part of the name is enough: "Adw" finds the same row.

steps.t: Tick the box at the start of the AdwCleaner row, then click Install selected at the top of the list.

steps.tip: If it failed, check the internet connection and click Install selected again; a second try often works when a download was interrupted. The full reason is in Reports, in the newest Install report.

steps.t: Windows: click the Start button (the Windows logo at the bottom of the screen), type AdwCleaner and click it when it appears at the top of the list.
steps.see: AdwCleaner opens in its own window. If a box asks "Do you want to allow this app to make changes to your device?", click Yes. That box is Windows checking with you, not an error.
steps.tip: If AdwCleaner does not appear straight away, wait a few seconds and type the name again, or look under All apps in the Start menu.

sections.heading: How to use it

steps.t: Close all browsers. Open AdwCleaner and Agree to the terms.
steps.see: A dashboard with Scan now.

steps.t: Click Scan now.
steps.see: Usually under a minute. Then a list of findings grouped by type.
ex: Services: 1 (eg. GoogleUpdaterService... (only if odd))
Folders: 3   C:\Program Files (x86)\Search Protect
Registry: 6   HKCU\Software\Conduit
Chromium extensions: 2   "Quick Maps Now"

steps: Leave everything ticked unless it is a program the person wants, and click Quarantine.

steps.t: Click Continue at the warning: programs will be closed.
steps.see: A request to restart the computer.

steps.t: Restart. After restarting, a log opens showing what was removed. Open each browser and check its home page and search engine are back to normal (Settings, Search engine). If not, reset the browser: in MendKit, use Clean browsers under Repair.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Items under Preinstalled software are things the computer maker added. Untick them if the person uses them.
Basic repair (under Settings) also resets browser policies and network settings; leave it at default unless the browser is still hijacked.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: AdwCleaner is free for personal use only. Using it on customers' computers as a business needs the paid licence from its maker.

steps.tip: If Hostname is blank, Tools, Fetchers lets you add MAC Vendor, which names the maker.
ex: 192.168.1.1    router.lan        TP-Link
192.168.1.42   HP2A1B3C          HP        ← the printer
192.168.1.57   Galaxy-S23        Samsung   ← a phone

steps: Hostname and MAC Vendor columns help identify each device (for example HP for a printer).

~/Library/Caches/us.zoom.xos

Clearing private browsing traces before passing a computer on.

steps.t: Wait until the Status column for GNU ddrescue says Installed and the bottom panel says the job has finished.

steps.t: GNU ddrescue has no window of its own: you type its commands in Terminal (Command Prompt or PowerShell on Windows). See the guide "Opening Terminal and typing a command" if you have not done this before.
steps.tip: If Terminal says "command not found" or "is not recognized", close Terminal and open a new one. A Terminal that was already open does not see newly installed programs.

sections.heading: How to use it

steps.t: Connect the failing drive and a healthy drive at least as large.
steps.warn: Everything on the healthy (destination) drive will be overwritten. Getting the source and destination the wrong way round destroys the files you are trying to save.

steps.t: Find both drives. Linux: sudo lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,MODEL   Mac: diskutil list
steps.see: Each drive with its size and model, such as sdb 500G and sdc 1T (Linux) or disk2 and disk3 (Mac). Write down which is which.
ex: Linux:
> sudo lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,MODEL
sda  238.5G  SAMSUNG MZ7LN256  ← the computer's own drive
sdb  465.8G  WDC WD5000LPVX   ← the failing drive (source)
sdc  931.5G  Seagate Expansion ← the healthy drive (destination)

steps: Unmount any volumes on them. Mac: diskutil unmountDisk /dev/disk2 (for each). Linux: they are not mounted if nothing opened them.

steps.t: First pass, fast, skipping bad areas. Linux: sudo ddrescue -n /dev/sdb /dev/sdc rescue.map   Mac: sudo ddrescue -n /dev/rdisk2 /dev/rdisk3 rescue.map
steps.see: A live status: rescued, bad areas, read errors and the time remaining.
steps.tip: First the failing drive, then the healthy one, then the log file name. The -f option may be needed to write to a whole drive: add -f before -n.
ex: > sudo ddrescue -f -n /dev/sdb /dev/sdc rescue.map
rescued: 401 GB, bad areas: 12, read errors: 340, pct rescued: 86.12%, remaining time: 1h 20m

steps.t: Second pass, retrying bad areas three times: same command with -r3 instead of -n.
ex: > sudo ddrescue -f -r3 /dev/sdb /dev/sdc rescue.map

steps: When finished, run TestDisk, PhotoRec, or MendKit's "Copy from an old drive" on the healthy copy, never on the failing drive.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: "pct rescued" near 100% is a near-complete copy. Bad areas show how much could not be read.
The rescue.map file lets you stop with Ctrl C and run the same command later to continue.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: If a drive makes clicking or grinding noises, every hour running can make it worse. For irreplaceable files, a professional lab is the safest choice.

steps: rkhunter (Rootkit Hunter) checks system files, hidden files and settings for signs of rootkits and tampering.

sections.heading: When to use it
steps: Suspected compromise of a Linux computer or server.

steps.t: Open MendKit. At the bottom left of its window, tick the Technician mode box.
steps.see: Repair, Tools and Tweaks appear in the menu on the left. If they were already there, Technician mode was already on.

steps.t: Click Tools in the menu on the left. Click the search box at the top of the list and type rkhunter.
steps.see: The list shrinks to the row for rkhunter: a tick box, its name, what it is for, its licence and a Status column saying Not installed or Installed.
ex: Part of the name is enough: "rkh" finds the same row.

steps.t: Tick the box at the start of the rkhunter row, then click Install selected at the top of the list.
steps.see: The panel at the bottom of MendKit shows each step of the download and install as it happens. It usually takes one to five minutes.

steps.t: Wait until the Status column for rkhunter says Installed and the bottom panel says the job has finished.
steps.tip: If it failed, check the internet connection and click Install selected again; a second try often works when a download was interrupted. The full reason is in Reports, in the newest Install report.

steps.t: rkhunter has no window of its own: you type its commands in Terminal (Command Prompt or PowerShell on Windows). See the guide "Opening Terminal and typing a command" if you have not done this before.
steps.tip: If Terminal says "command not found" or "is not recognized", close Terminal and open a new one. A Terminal that was already open does not see newly installed programs.

sections.heading: How to use it
steps: Update its data: sudo rkhunter --update
Record the current system as the baseline: sudo rkhunter --propupd

steps.t: Run the check: sudo rkhunter --check --sk
steps.see: Many checks with OK, Not found or Warning.

steps.t: Read the summary and the warnings: sudo grep Warning /var/log/rkhunter.log
ex: Warning: The file properties have changed: File: /usr/bin/curl  ← normal after updating curl; run sudo rkhunter --propupd after updates
Warning: Hidden directory found: /etc/.java  ← usually harmless
Warning: Found possible rootkit files  ← take seriously

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Warnings are often false alarms after normal updates (changed file properties). A warning about a known rootkit or a hidden process deserves expert attention.

title: smartmontools
summary: Reads a drive's own health records (SMART) and runs its built-in self-tests.

sections.heading: What it is
steps: Every hard drive and SSD keeps a health record: errors, bad areas, hours used and wear. smartmontools reads it with the smartctl command.
MendKit's drive health checks use it on Mac and Linux.

sections.heading: When to use it
steps: A computer is slow, freezes, or makes clicking noises.
Before trusting an old or second-hand drive with someone's files.
MendKit says a drive is not Healthy and you want the details.

steps.t: Open MendKit. At the bottom left of its window, tick the Technician mode box.
steps.see: Repair, Tools and Tweaks appear in the menu on the left. If they were already there, Technician mode was already on.

steps.t: Click Tools in the menu on the left. Click the search box at the top of the list and type smartmontools.
steps.see: The list shrinks to the row for smartmontools: a tick box, its name, what it is for, its licence and a Status column saying Not installed or Installed.
ex: Part of the name is enough: "sma" finds the same row.

steps.t: Tick the box at the start of the smartmontools row, then click Install selected at the top of the list.
steps.see: The panel at the bottom of MendKit shows each step of the download and install as it happens. It usually takes one to five minutes.
steps.tip: On Windows, click "Restart as administrator" on the Dashboard first, so installs do not stop half-way to ask permission. On a Mac or Linux, MendKit asks for your password once; nothing shows on screen as you type it, which is normal.

steps.t: Wait until the Status column for smartmontools says Installed and the bottom panel says the job has finished.
steps.tip: If it failed, check the internet connection and click Install selected again; a second try often works when a download was interrupted. The full reason is in Reports, in the newest Install report.

steps.t: smartmontools has no window of its own: you type its commands in Terminal (Command Prompt or PowerShell on Windows). See the guide "Opening Terminal and typing a command" if you have not done this before.
steps.tip: If Terminal says "command not found" or "is not recognized", close Terminal and open a new one. A Terminal that was already open does not see newly installed programs.

steps.t: Open Terminal as administrator (Windows), or a normal Terminal on a Mac or Linux. On Windows, click Start, type cmd, right-click Command Prompt and choose Run as administrator.
List the drives: smartctl --scan
steps.see: Lines such as /dev/sda or /dev/nvme0 (Linux), /dev/disk0 (Mac), /dev/sda or /dev/nvme0 (Windows).
ex: > smartctl --scan
/dev/sda -d ata # /dev/sda, ATA device
/dev/nvme0 -d nvme # /dev/nvme0, NVMe device
Each line is one drive. Use the first word (here /dev/sda or /dev/nvme0) in the next command.

steps.t: Read the health of the first drive. Windows and Linux: sudo smartctl -a /dev/sda (leave out sudo on Windows). Mac: sudo smartctl -a disk0. The output is long: scroll up to the line that starts with SMART overall-health, then down to the table of numbers.
steps.see: Several screens of information. The key line is "SMART overall-health self-assessment test result: PASSED".
ex: Linux, first drive:
> sudo smartctl -a /dev/sda
Windows, NVMe drive:
> smartctl -a /dev/nvme0
Mac, internal drive:
> sudo smartctl -a disk0
To show only the health line and the error counts:
> sudo smartctl -H -A /dev/sda

steps.t: Optional: start a short self-test: sudo smartctl -t short /dev/sda. Wait the minutes it says, then read the result: sudo smartctl -l selftest /dev/sda
steps.tip: "Completed: read failure" with a number in the last column means the test found a bad area at that place on the drive. Back up now.
ex: > sudo smartctl -t short /dev/sda
Please wait 2 minutes for test to complete.
Then:
> sudo smartctl -l selftest /dev/sda
# 1  Short offline   Completed without error   00%   12345   -

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: PASSED does not guarantee a healthy drive; also read the numbers below.
Hard drives: Reallocated_Sector_Ct, Current_Pending_Sector or Offline_Uncorrectable above 0 mean the surface is failing. Back up now.
SSDs: "Percentage Used" near or over 100%, or "Available Spare" below the threshold, mean it is worn out. "Media and Data Integrity Errors" above 0 is a bad sign.
Power_On_Hours shows the drive's age in hours (8,760 is one year switched on).

sections.heading: If something goes wrong
steps: "Unable to detect device type": add -d sat for a USB drive, for example smartctl -a -d sat /dev/sdb.
Many USB enclosures hide SMART data entirely. Connect the drive directly if you can.

steps.t: Stop using the drive or card with the lost files straight away.
steps.warn: Every new file written to it can overwrite what you want back. Never recover files onto the same drive they came from.

steps: Plug in a second drive with plenty of free space for the recovered files.

steps.t: Open Terminal as administrator and type photorec (sudo photorec on Mac and Linux). On Windows you can also double-click photorec_win.exe in its folder.
steps.see: A list of drives with their sizes. A text screen headed PhotoRec with a list of disks and a row of choices at the bottom ([Proceed] [Quit]). The mouse does nothing here: use the arrow keys and Enter.
ex: Windows (in the folder where it was installed):
> photorec_win
Mac and Linux:
> sudo photorec

steps.t: Use the arrow keys to choose the drive or card with the lost files, and press Enter. Then press the right arrow to highlight [Proceed] if needed, and press Enter.
steps.tip: Pick by size: a 64 GB card shows as about 62 GB.
ex: Disk /dev/sda - 512 GB / 476 GiB (the computer's own drive)
Disk /dev/sdb - 63 GB / 59 GiB - Generic STORAGE DEVICE (a 64 GB memory card)

steps.t: Choose the partition (or "No partition" for the whole thing) and press Enter on Search. The screen lists the partitions on the drive; usually there is one large one (FAT32, exFAT or NTFS). Highlight it and press Enter. Use [File Opt] first if you only want certain types: press s to untick all, then tick jpg, mov or docx with the Space key, and press b to save.

steps: Choose the file system type: Other for Windows drives and memory cards, ext2/ext3 for Linux.

steps.t: Choose Whole to search everything (Free only searches unused space, faster).
steps.tip: Free is faster and enough when files were deleted from a drive that is still in use. Choose Whole for a formatted card or a drive that says it needs formatting.

steps.t: Move to the second drive's folder where the files should go and press C to choose it. Use the arrow keys and Enter to open folders; .. goes up one level. When you are inside the folder you want, press C (capital or small) to start.
steps.see: A counter of files found by type. It can take hours.
ex: Windows: move up to C:, then into the other drive, for example E:\Recovered
Mac: /Volumes/Backup/Recovered
Linux: /media/yourname/Backup/Recovered

steps.t: When it finishes, open the destination folder.
steps.see: Folders named recup_dir.1, recup_dir.2 and so on, full of files with numbered names.

sections.heading: Lost partition: TestDisk
steps: Type testdisk (sudo testdisk on Mac/Linux). Choose Create for a log, pick the drive, accept the detected partition type, then Analyse and Quick Search.

steps.t: If the lost partition is listed in green, press Enter, then choose Write and confirm with Y. Restart the computer.
steps.warn: Writing changes the partition table. If unsure, copy the files out instead: highlight the partition and press P to list and copy them.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: PhotoRec loses original file names and folders. Sort the recovered files by type or date, and use a photo viewer to find the ones wanted.

sections.heading: If something goes wrong
steps: A drive that clicks, is not detected, or is extremely slow is physically failing: stop, and use ddrescue to copy it first, or send it to a data recovery lab.

summary: Shows what is using the space on a drive, as a colour map of every file.

sections.heading: What it is
steps: WinDirStat scans a drive and shows folders largest first, plus a map where each rectangle is a file sized by how big it is.

sections.heading: When to use it
steps: The drive is full and you do not know why.
Finding forgotten large files: old videos, game installers, backups.

steps.t: Open MendKit. At the bottom left of its window, tick the Technician mode box.
steps.see: Repair, Tools and Tweaks appear in the menu on the left. If they were already there, Technician mode was already on.

steps.t: Click Tools in the menu on the left. Click the search box at the top of the list and type WinDirStat.
steps.see: The list shrinks to the row for WinDirStat: a tick box, its name, what it is for, its licence and a Status column saying Not installed or Installed.
ex: Part of the name is enough: "Win" finds the same row.

steps.t: Tick the box at the start of the WinDirStat row, then click Install selected at the top of the list.
steps.see: The panel at the bottom of MendKit shows each step of the download and install as it happens. It usually takes one to five minutes.
steps.tip: On Windows, click "Restart as administrator" on the Dashboard first, so installs do not stop half-way to ask permission. On a Mac or Linux, MendKit asks for your password once; nothing shows on screen as you type it, which is normal.

steps.t: Wait until the Status column for WinDirStat says Installed and the bottom panel says the job has finished.
steps.tip: If it failed, check the internet connection and click Install selected again; a second try often works when a download was interrupted. The full reason is in Reports, in the newest Install report.

steps.t: Windows: click the Start button (the Windows logo at the bottom of the screen), type WinDirStat and click it when it appears at the top of the list.
steps.see: WinDirStat opens in its own window. If a box asks "Do you want to allow this app to make changes to your device?", click Yes. That box is Windows checking with you, not an error.
steps.tip: If WinDirStat does not appear straight away, wait a few seconds and type the name again, or look under All apps in the Start menu.

steps.t: Open WinDirStat.
steps.see: A box asking which drives to scan.

steps.t: Choose the C: drive (or All Local Drives) and click OK.
steps.see: Pac-Man icons while it scans, which can take a few minutes. Then a folder list at the top and the colour map below.
steps.tip: Scanning all drives can take a long time with a large external drive plugged in. Start with C: only.

steps.t: Click the arrow beside the biggest folders in the list to open them, largest first.
ex: A typical full drive:
C:\Users\Ann\Videos   86 GB (old phone videos)
C:\Users\Ann\AppData\Local\Packages   24 GB (app data, leave it)
C:\Windows   28 GB (Windows itself, leave it)
C:\Users\Ann\Downloads   19 GB (old installers, usually safe to clear)

steps.t: Click a large rectangle in the map to find which file it is. The list at the top jumps to that file and highlights it. The colour shows the file type; the legend on the right says which colour is which (for example .mp4 videos, .iso disk images).
To delete something, right-click it and choose Delete (to Recycle Bin).
steps.warn: Do not delete anything inside Windows, Program Files, ProgramData or AppData unless you know what it is. Uninstall programs the normal way instead.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Huge pagefile.sys and hiberfil.sys files belong to Windows and are normal.
A large folder under Users is personal files: ask before deleting.
Windows.old (after an upgrade) can be removed with Disk Cleanup, Clean up system files.

summary: Captures and shows network traffic packet by packet.

sections.heading: What it is
steps: Wireshark records the network traffic passing through a computer and shows every message. A specialist tool for network problems.

steps.see: The panel at the bottom of MendKit shows each step of the download and install as it happens. It usually takes one to five minutes.

steps.tip: If macOS says the developer cannot be verified, open System Settings, Privacy & Security, scroll down and click Open Anyway.

steps.tip: Programs installed as a Flatpak can take a minute to appear in the menu. If it is not there, sign out and back in.

sections.heading: How to use it

steps.t: Open Wireshark.
steps.see: A list of network interfaces with small live activity graphs.

steps.t: Double-click the interface with activity (Wi-Fi or Ethernet).
steps.see: Packets scrolling past.

steps: Reproduce the problem, then click the red square to stop.

steps.t: Type a filter in the bar at the top and press Enter, for example dns, or ip.addr == 192.168.1.1.
ex: dns                       only name lookups
ip.addr == 192.168.1.1    traffic to or from the router
tcp.analysis.flags        problems such as retransmissions
http || tls               web traffic

steps: File, Save As to keep the capture for a technician.

sections.heading: Reading the results
steps: Red or black rows are errors such as retransmissions or resets.

sections.heading: Take care
steps: Captures can contain private information. Only capture on networks you own, and share files only with someone you trust.
